We went out a little later than usual and walked down the lane behind the market. The gulmohar near the corner has started flowering again, bright red on top. A koel was calling from somewhere near the temple, the same as last time. There were puddles everywhere because it rained in the afternoon. The park was quite full, children were playing near the swings. I think we saw a kingfisher by the pond, but it flew away very fast. Two dogs followed us for a while and then went back to the tea stall. The air smelled of wet earth and somebody was frying pakoras. We sat on the bench near the gate for a few minutes and rested. The neem tree by the school has lost a big branch in the storm. Some kind of small brown bird was hopping on the footpath. We met the man who sells flowers, and he said the jasmine is late this year. The sky turned orange and then grey, and the street lights came on. Near the bus stop there were three parrots sitting on the wire. The road by the lake is being repaired, so we took the longer way round. Maybe it was a mynah, it had a yellow patch near the eye. We could hear the temple bells from the far end of the park.
